question: Will the US and China announce an extension of their tariff truce during or immediately after the September 2026 Madrid trade talks?

calls.reasoning: The question needs an explicit, confirmed extension announcement dated Sept 17-19, 2026 - a 3-day window one week before the Sept 24 Trump-Xi White House summit that every source treats as the decision venue. USTR has publicly framed announcements as coming 'during the summit'; the early-September ministerial round was explicitly described as preparing summit deliverables, which is the opposite of pre-empting them. The Nov 10 expiry is still ~2 months away, Bessent said in May the US is 'not in a rush,' Washington was reported in late August to be readying a new 7.5% overcapacity tariff before the summit, and the two sides still disagree on duration (China reportedly wants through 2029). Historically these ministerial rounds issue 'consensus/framework' readouts and leave the concrete truce action to leaders or to later executive instruments; the fine print explicitly excludes intent/optimism/plan language. I also could not confirm a Madrid round exists on those 2026 dates - the overwhelming majority of Madrid coverage is the September 2025 round - which adds premise risk on the NO side. An extension being 'almost certain' eventually is well-supported; landing it inside this specific window is not.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off an official statement/readout/fact sheet/press release from MOFCOM, US Treasury, USTR or the White House (or credible reporting of one) that explicitly announces an AGREED extension of the tariff truce beyond its Nov 10, 2026 expiry, or specifies a new end date later than Nov 10, 2026. It does NOT resolve off expressions of intent, optimism, or a plan to decide later; nor off TikTok, soybean, or rare-earth announcements standing alone.

EVENT WINDOW: Sept 17, 2026 -> Sept 19, 2026 inclusive, per the criteria text. As of Now (2026-09-08T06:27Z), 0% elapsed; the window opens in ~8.7 days and lasts 3 days. An extension agreed and announced before Sept 17 does not count.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: no qualifying official announcement is issued in the three-day window; the truce's future remains on the table for the Sept 24 leaders' meeting, with the Nov 10 expiry still ~7.5 weeks beyond the window's close.

EVIDENCE (both directions):
- Treasury Sec. Bessent, Reuters exclusive, May 19-20, 2026: US is 'not in a hurry' to extend the truce ending in November; said there is time to renew it in meetings later in the year (japantimes.co.jp, 2026-05-20).
- Bessent, same interview: expects China to accept restoration of prior US tariff rates via new Section 301 duties so long as they do not go higher; called China's critical-minerals compliance 'satisfactory, but not excellent.'
- Bloomberg, Aug 24, 2026: US weighing a 7.5% overcapacity tariff on Chinese goods BEFORE the Xi-Trump summit, sized to fill headroom under a 20% cap Washington committed to China's Commerce Ministry on July 27, 2026; Beijing has said 20% total is consistent with the truce.
- SCMP, Aug 28, 2026: sources describe the one-year Busan (Oct 2025) agreement as likely to be extended; Chinese executives may join Xi's delegation. Article's focus is the Sept 24 Washington meeting as the diplomatic moment; no Madrid reference.
- Reporting (Aug-Sept 2026): Bessent, USTR Greer and Vice Premier He Lifeng were to meet in early September to discuss summit DELIVERABLES; USTR said the two countries will make 'some announcements on agriculture and non-tariff barriers' DURING the summit, without specifics.
- Trump-Xi White House state visit confirmed for Sept 24, 2026, aligned with UNGA; first Chinese state visit to Washington in over a decade; formal state dinner planned. China had not officially confirmed at the time of early-Sept reporting.
- Qz (Sept 3, 2026) and CNBC (Sept 2, 2026) headlines: expectations for the Sept 24 summit are LOW; analysts say it is likely to manage rather than resolve tensions, with Iran sanctions and tariffs clouding the agenda.
- Fortune/PBS/Washington Times, Sept 1-2, 2026: at the G20 finance track, Bessent said 19 of 20 finance ministers agreed to address 'cheap exports'; China dissented - an active friction point days before the window.
- CSIS 'Trump-Xi 2026 Summits' page: May 2026 Beijing summit produced a cooperation framework and agricultural purchase pledges; deeper tech tensions (AI, export controls, cyber) explicitly unresolved. CSIS scheduled a press briefing for Sept 17, 2026 to PREVIEW the meeting and a follow-up analysis for Sept 25 - i.e. outside analysts treat Sept 17 as pre-summit, not decision day.
- Prior-round pattern: Geneva (May 2025), London (June 2025), Stockholm (July 2025), Madrid (Sept 2025), Kuala Lumpur (Oct 2025), Seoul (May 2026), Paris (Mar 2026). Stockholm produced an agreement 'in principle' to extend 90 days, with the formal extension to Nov 10 announced ~2 weeks later (Aug 11-12, 2025) by presidential action. The Kuala Lumpur/Busan sequence had the ministerial round produce a framework and the LEADERS announce the one-year truce.
- Madrid Sept 2025 precedent (the round the background cites): ministerial readouts covered US tariff measures, 'abuse' of export controls and TikTok; the headline deliverable was a TikTok framework, not a truce extension - the Nov 10 date had already been set in August 2025.

BASE RATES:
- Over all ~7-8 ministerial US-China rounds since May 2025: roughly 2 were followed within 3 days by an official announcement that the truce was extended/rolled over - and in both, the operative announcement came from leaders or a presidential instrument rather than the ministerial readout itself.
- Over rounds held with a leaders' summit scheduled within ~2 weeks AFTER (Kuala Lumpur->Busan; Seoul->Beijing): the concrete tariff outcome was announced at the leaders' meeting, not at the ministerial round, in both observed cases.
- Over rounds held with the truce deadline more than 6 weeks away: no observed case of an extension being announced at that round.

DECIDING-BODY CALENDAR: Trump-Xi state visit Sept 24, 2026, White House (confirmed by US side; Chinese confirmation reported as pending in early Sept). Truce expiry 12:01 a.m. EST Nov 10, 2026; Section 301 exclusions run to the same date. MOFCOM issues spokesperson remarks on consultations typically within 1-2 days of a round's close; Treasury posts press releases and travel announcements at home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases. No published MOFCOM or USTR bulletin calendar fixing an announcement to Sept 17-19 was found.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: (1) any independent 2026-dated confirmation that a US-China round is scheduled in Madrid on Sept 14-17, 2026 - essentially all Madrid-dated coverage retrieved is the September 2025 round (Bessent's Sept 12-18 Europe trip to Spain and the UK, He Lifeng's Sept 14-17 delegation, the Windsor state visit) and the only 2026-confirmed item is an unlocated 'early September' Bessent/Greer/He meeting on summit deliverables; (2) any MOFCOM or Treasury/USTR readout dated September 2026 on a Spain round; (3) any published statement from either government committing to announce the truce decision before the Sept 24 summit; (4) any prediction market whose contract matches these resolution terms.

calls.reasoning: Two hurdles must both clear. (1) I could not verify that the asserted Sept 14-17, 2026 Madrid round exists at all — every trace of 'Madrid, Sept 14-17, He/Bessent' dates to 2025, and the 2026 pre-summit contact reported by Reuters (Sept 4) already occurred in 'early September' at an undetermined location. Call it ~30% that a high-level round actually convenes in that window. (2) Even conditional on it happening, the reference class of US-China truce-deadline events says formal extensions are announced at leader level or by executive order near the deadline (Aug 11 2025 EO, one day before expiry; Nov 10 2025 EO after Busan), while ministerial rounds produce frameworks and 'preliminary consensus subject to leaders' — precisely what this question's fine print excludes. Madrid 2025 itself produced a TikTok framework and no truce extension. Nov 10 is still ~9 weeks out, Bessent said the US is 'not in a rush,' the sides disagree on duration (US ~1 year vs China through 2029), and Trump has strong incentive to hold the deliverable for the Sept 24 White House summit — which Greer on Sept 4 framed as the venue for announcements. That gives ~25% YES given talks, ~4% absent them. No matching human market exists to move me off this.

- July 30-31, 2026: Bessent + Greer held a >1hr video call with He Lifeng; He raised "serious concern" over new US curbs; both sides agreed to enhance communication ahead of Xi's September visit (Bloomberg / SCMP / Axios, Jul 30-Aug 2, 2026).

- Aug 28, 2026 (SCMP exclusive): sources say the Busan one-year deal is "likely to be extended"; Chinese executives may join Xi's US delegation. Article does not state where or when an extension would be announced.

- Sept 3, 2026: Trump says he is "excited" about Xi's Washington visit.
- Sept 4, 2026 (Reuters exclusive): Bessent, Greer and He Lifeng met in EARLY September to discuss summit deliverables; Reuters could not determine the date or location. Same day, Greer said he expects announcements on a Board of Trade and US agricultural sales during Xi's Washington visit.

- Reported sticking point: duration. US side reportedly favors ~one year; China reportedly wants an extension running to 2029.
- Trump-Xi summit set for Sept 24, 2026 at the White House, timed to UNGA (CSIS 2026 summit tracker); widely framed as a low-expectations, stalemate-management meeting.

EVIDENCE — the asserted Madrid round:
- I could not corroborate any Sept 14-17, 2026 Madrid round. Every retrievable 'Madrid / Sept 14-17 / He Lifeng / Bessent / Li Chenggang / Palacio de Santa Cruz' item dates to 2025: MOFCOM announced He's Spain trip on Sept 12, 2025 (gov.cn), talks ran Sept 14-17, 2025 and concluded 'constructive' (China Daily, Sept 16, 2025).
- As of Sept 8, 2026 there is no MOFCOM announcement of a delegation to Spain; the 2025 analogue was announced two days before travel, so absence now is not dispositive.
- SCMP's US-China trade-war topic page (latest items Aug 31-Sept 4, 2026) and Global Times' front page carry no mention of a 2026 Madrid/Spain round.

Kuala Lumpur's MOFCOM readout did enumerate a preliminary-consensus list including a one-year reciprocal-tariff suspension extension, which is the closest historical near-miss to this criterion.

- Over the 2025 Madrid round specifically (the direct precedent named in the question background): outcome was a TikTok framework; no tariff-truce extension was announced there — the Nov 10 deadline then in force was left untouched until Busan/Oct 30.

Treasury press-release page and USTR publish readouts at the conclusion of ministerial rounds, typically same-day or next-day. UNGA high-level week and the Sept 24 White House summit sit immediately after the window. Any US extension of the reciprocal-tariff suspension has historically required a presidential executive action; searched for a scheduled date for such an action and found none.

calls.reasoning: Needs a confirmed-agreement announcement dated Sept 17-19, 2026 — a three-day window sitting one week before the Sept 24 Trump-Xi White House state visit that every source treats as the decision venue. Greer (Sept 4) framed announcements as coming 'during the summit'; the early-September ministerial was explicitly about summit deliverables, i.e. pre-cooking rather than pre-empting them. Nov 10 is ~7.5 weeks past the window, so no forcing deadline; Bessent said in May the US is 'not in a rush'; the sides are still apart on duration (US ~1yr vs China to 2029), the exact parameter leaders settle. Base rate for rounds immediately preceding a leaders' summit with the deadline weeks out is 0/2 (Madrid 2025 -> Busan; Paris 2026 -> Beijing). I sit above the three runs (0.08/0.09/0.11) for two reasons: I do not apply Run 2's ~70% premise discount on the Madrid round (the Background asserts it, and Reuters corroborates an early-September ministerial), and I weight the Kuala-Lumpur channel higher — a MOFCOM readout enumerating 'consensus reached' on extending the suspension, reported by wires as an agreed extension, plausibly clears the 'credible reporting' clause even if formally pending the summit. That ambiguity, not a genuine Madrid decision, is where most of my YES mass lives.
calls.reconciliation: Two disputes drove the spread. FACTUAL: whether a Sept 14-17, 2026 Madrid round exists — all three runs failed to corroborate it (search returns dominated by the 2025 namesake), and Run 2 applied a ~30% probability that any round convenes, which is most of why it sat at 0.09. I could not settle this by search (no web access this run), but the question Background asserts the round as fact and Reuters (Sept 4, 2026) independently reports a Bessent/Greer/He meeting in early September at an undetermined location; I carry the premise at ~0.85 rather than 0.30, which raises my number relative to Run 2. JUDGMENT, unbroken by evidence: how a Kuala-Lumpur-style readout ('preliminary consensus' including a one-year extension, pending leaders) resolves. Runs 1 and 2 score it NO on the fine print excluding intent and plans-to-decide; Run 3 flags it as the main offset. The criteria also accept 'reporting by credible sources of such an official announcement,' and wires did report Kuala Lumpur as an agreed one-year truce extension — so I weight this channel higher than any run did. That is the bet I would take, not a settled fact. SETTLED and agreed across runs: Greer designated the Sept 24 summit as the announcement venue; the duration gap (US ~1yr vs China to 2029) is unresolved; the Nov 10 expiry exerts no pressure this far out; and no prediction market matches the criteria (the nearest Polymarket contract differs on deadline, instrument and fine print, so it is evidence rather than an anchor). Net: the premise correction and the fine-print correction both push up, so I land modestly above all three runs rather than between them.
